chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal ibn Jameel, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said:

Be quiet as long as the heavens and the earth are quiet (i.e., do not rise up against anyone), for your matter is not obscure. Indeed, it is a sign from Allah, not from people, but it is brighter than the sun. It does not hide from the pious nor from the dissolute. Do you know the dawn? Indeed, it is like the dawn, which is not obscure.

key_terms.أَضْوَأُ مِنَ الشَّمْسِ: Brighter than the sun (metaphor for clarity)
key_terms.أَمْرَكُمْ: Your matter/affair (referring to the cause or event)
key_terms.سَكَنتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ: The heavens and the earth are quiet (a metaphor for a period of waiting or calm)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'Be quiet as long as the heavens and the earth are quiet'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) advises patience and waiting for the right moment, comparing the clarity of the upcoming event to the dawn which is unmistakable to all. He emphasizes that the matter is clear and known to both the righteous and the wicked, so there is no need to force a premature uprising. This narration underscores the concept of *al-Ghayba al-Sughra* (Minor Occultation) context, where the Imam reassures followers that divine timing is precise and visible, discouraging the impatience that often leads to failed uprisings.
